options.name: avigail
options.description:
Plan verifier — bug-hunts in a brief BEFORE it goes to eliezer (executor). Reads the brief independently, validates every symbol/API/file:line claim against the actual codebase, checks pseudo-code for missing branches and type errors, flags naming inconsistencies and outdated risks. Validates that depends_on is declared and consistent with the brief. Catches problems that would cost the executor 30-60 min of debug or worse — silent regressions.
Track record: 100% of 3 briefs verified had at least one real issue, avg 3 issues per brief. Cost ~10 min, saves 30-60 min downstream.
Invoke with: Task(subagent_type="avigail", prompt="...")
The prompt MUST include: brief path, project root (dev tip), what symbols/APIs the brief claims exist. If brief path is missing, refuse.

options.name: calev
options.description:
Runtime verifier (Sonnet) — checks that the executor's work actually works in a real environment. Handles the two lightweight tiers via the `mode:` field in the dispatch prompt:
- mode: phase   — Lightweight check after a single phase (~10-15 min).
                  Decides if next phase is blocked.
- mode: light   — End-of-slice check. Walks DoD items, runs 1-2 happy
                  paths, writes a short report (~15 min). Default tier.

For complexity 8+ slices use calev-heavy (Opus) instead — the heavy 7-stage protocol is inference-heavy (edge cases, regressions, patterns) and pays for the higher model. This agent (Sonnet) covers phase/light, where the truth comes from runtime, not inference.
Does NOT edit code. Reads brief independently (does NOT trust executor framing). Reports what it finds in the real running environment.
The prompt MUST include: brief path, slice name, commit hash, environment notes, AND `mode: <phase|light>`. If brief path is missing, refuse and ask.
Invoke with: Task(subagent_type="calev", prompt="...") For heavy: Task(subagent_type="calev-heavy", prompt="...")

options.name: calev-heavy
options.description:
Runtime verifier — HEAVY tier (complexity 8+). Same role as calev (runtime verification in a real environment), but runs on Opus because the heavy protocol is inference-heavy, not just runtime: edge-case hunting (imagining what was NOT tested), regression hunting (holding the whole system in mind), and patterns classification — all reasoning work where Opus pays off. The phase/light tiers stay on calev (Sonnet) since there the truth comes from runtime, not inference.
Full 7-stage protocol: visual review (mobile+desktop), E2E flows, edge cases, regressions, patterns classification, tagged JSON report.
Does NOT edit code. Reads brief independently (does NOT trust executor framing). Reports what it finds in the real running environment.
The prompt MUST include: brief path, slice name, commit hash, environment notes. (mode is implicitly heavy — this IS the heavy agent.) If brief path is missing, refuse and ask.
Invoke with: Task(subagent_type="calev-heavy", prompt="...")

options.name: eliezer
options.description:
Implementation agent — executes a brief phase-by-phase. Testing approach per phase comes FROM the brief (tdd / integration / manual / none), not assumed. Sonnet-level. Stops and reports when stuck (does NOT try to solve architectural problems on its own). Invokes calev (runtime-verifier) after UI/data-flow/route phases. Invokes calev at the end of each slice.
Can run as subagent (via Task from Mordechai) or as primary session (via opencode run --agent eliezer, dispatched by Yetro in tmux). In Mode 2 (tmux/async), writes outcomes/<slice>.json (status=blocked or completed) instead of returning a Task result.
Invoke with: Task(subagent_type="eliezer", prompt="...") OR: opencode run --agent eliezer < prompt.txt (via dispatch-executor.sh)
The prompt must include: brief path, slice name, environment notes (which ports run what, where the browser is, what the test fixtures are).

options.name: mordechai
options.description:
Strategic planner — writes detailed briefs, reviews brief verification reports from Avigail (plan-verifier), dispatches Eliezer (executor) or Yetro (orchestrator), and is the ONLY agent authorized to merge branches into dev after explicit user approval.
Mordechai sees the full roadmap and makes architectural decisions. Eliezer executes. Yetro orchestrates the queue. Avigail catches plan mistakes. Calev verifies runtime behavior.
This is a primary session agent — start a session with agent=mordechai for strategic planning, brief writing, morning reviews, and merges.

options.name: yetro
options.description:
Orchestrator — runs the nightly slice queue automatically. Dispatches Eliezer (executor) via tmux, polls for completion, runs Calev (verifier), archives passing briefs, and writes a morning summary for Mordechai.
Yetro is intentionally "dumb and safe": he does NOT make architectural decisions, does NOT merge, does NOT fix failures — he stops and documents. Mordechai reads the summary in the morning and decides what to do.
Start a Yetro session from the orchestration-project directory. Yetro reads projects.json to know which projects to process. One Yetro per project (enforced by flock on yetro.lock).
Invoke: open a session with agent=yetro from ~/projects/orchestration/

availableCommands.name: commit
availableCommands.description:
Structured git commit workflow for this user's projects. Includes:
pre-flight `npm run check` (or `/watch-check`), Walkthrough doc update,
selective `git add` (no blanket adds), one git command at a time
(no chained `&&`), commit-message style, and Hebrew commit messages.

Use when the user asks to:
- "commit", "make a commit", "תעשה קומיט", "תקמט"
- "commit and push" (this skill handles commit; push only if asked)
- Wrap up a feature / fix and record it in git
- Run the standard pre-commit checks before committing

This is NOT a generic git wrapper — it enforces a specific multi-step
workflow (check → walkthrough → status → diff → add → commit) and uses
Hebrew for commit messages. Do not use for one-off `git commit` calls
where the user just wants a quick commit.

Triggers when user mentions:
- "commit", "קומיט", "תקמט", "תעשה קומיט"
- "מקדם" (in development context)
- "סיימתי, תשמור"

availableCommands.name: git-worktree-shared-assets
availableCommands.description:
Set up Windows Junction links so a freshly-created git worktree can access
large untracked static assets (images, sounds, videos, datasets) that live
in the source workspace and are gitignored. Without this, the worktree
is missing those files because Git doesn't track them.

Use AFTER creating a new worktree (e.g. via the `using-git-worktrees` flow)
when:
- The new worktree is missing assets (images, audio, video, fixtures, etc.)
- The user reports "the worktree is missing files"
- You see references to files that exist in the source repo but not the
  worktree, and they're listed in `.gitignore`

Windows-only (uses `mklink /J` Junction Points). For Linux/macOS, use
symlinks manually.

Triggers when user mentions:
- "git worktree" + missing assets
- "shared assets", "untracked files in worktree"
- "junction", "mklink", "symlink to source workspace"
- "the worktree doesn't have my images / sounds / videos"
